title: Rainfall deficits gave no clear repeated warmth interaction in English trout catches in 1991-2024
abstract: We tested whether low summer rainfall made the link between summer warmth and next-year trout catch more negative. A new panel used 5,153 complete electric-fishing surveys at 547 English sites in 1991-2024. Four main fits used 5,035 surveys after singleton removal, split between North and South and two time periods. Models controlled site, regional year, survey month, method, area and current weather. The warmth by rainfall-deficit estimates were -0.358, +0.041, +0.048 and -0.013 log catch-density units per C per SD. All four ordinary and four-test corrected intervals included zero. Controls left only 3-7% of the raw interaction variation. Adding future weather gave no clear previous-minus-future contrast in any sample. Survey checks did not show a repeated negative interaction. This result does not establish an absent effect or safe weather. Coarse air and rainfall proxies, selected surveys, capture bias and 14-18 year clusters limit inference. No water-flow, air-pollution or causal climate-change effect was tested. The bundle preserves code, aggregate results, figures, source hashes and numerical checks. All source records and derivative survey and weather tables stay external under their source terms.

display.caption: Previous-summer warmth by rainfall-deficit estimates for recorded trout catch density. Thick lines show ordinary 95% intervals. Thin lines show simultaneous four-test intervals. All include zero. The early North fit contains 1993-2006 records within the stated 1991-2006 bin.
The variation in the interaction term that remained after all other model terms and fixed effects. Only 3-7% remained. This is a measure of the fitted design, not of an ecological effect.

Planned survey and time checks for the previous-summer product. Points show estimates. Lines show ordinary 95% intervals. These checks did not give a repeated clear negative interaction in all four samples.
